name: Arpachshad
title: Shem's son and patriarch in the lineage of the Messiah
summary: Arpachshad was the son of Shem and grandson of Noah, born two years after the great flood when Shem was 100 years old. He is regarded as the first named person born in the world after the flood, thus representing a new beginning for humanity. According to the Hebrew base text, he became the father of Shelah at age 35 and lived to be 438 years old. Arpachshad is a central link in the genealogy from Noah through Shem to Abraham and onward to Jesus Christ. In the Septuagint and in Luke 3:36, an extra generation, Cainan, is placed between Arpachshad and Shelah—a difference that constitutes one of the best-known textual-critical questions related to biblical genealogies.

keyEvents.title: Born Two Years After the Flood
keyEvents.description: Arpachshad was born two years after the great flood as a son of Shem, when he was 100 years old. He is the first named person born in the new world after the flood.

keyEvents.title: Listed in the Table of Nations
keyEvents.description: Arpachshad is mentioned among the sons of Shem in the Table of Nations in Genesis 10, which describes how the nations spread out after the flood.

keyEvents.title: Father of Shelah
keyEvents.description: Arpachshad became the father of Shelah when he was 35 years old and lived for another 403 years after Shelah's birth – a total lifespan of 438 years.

keyEvents.title: The Lineage from Shem to Abraham
keyEvents.description: Arpachshad is listed in Shem's genealogy in Genesis 11, showing the messianic line from Shem through Arpachshad and Shelah onward to Abraham.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Genealogy of Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Arpachshad is included in the extensive genealogy in 1 Chronicles that connects Israel's history back to the beginning of humanity.

keyEvents.title: In Jesus' Lineage According to Luke
keyEvents.description: Arpachshad is mentioned in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, which traces Jesus' ancestry all the way back to Adam. Here, Cainan is also mentioned between Arpachshad and Shelah.

It is not wrong to include it, but verses 17 and 24 address different contexts within the chapter. Verse 17 lists the sons of Shem, verse 18 mentions Arpachshad as father of Shelah, and verse 24 restates the line from Shem. footnotes.text: The name Arpachshad (Hebrew: אַרְפַּכְשַׁד, ʾArpakšad) has an uncertain etymology. Some scholars have suggested a connection to the Akkadian "Arrapḫa" (modern-day Kirkuk in Iraq), while others see a link to the Chaldeans (kasdim). Josephus (Ant. 1.6.4) identifies Arpachshad as the ancestor of the Chaldeans.

In the Septuagint and in Luke 3:36, Cainan is mentioned as the son of Arpachshad and father of Shelah, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic text omits Cainan and makes Shelah the direct son of Arpachshad. This is one of the most discussed textual-critical differences between the two textual traditions.

According to Genesis 11:12–13, Arpachshad became the father of Shelah when he was 35 years old and lived for another 403 years – a total lifespan of 438 years. This places him in the gradually declining life expectancy curve after the flood, where the ages of the patriarchs decrease from Noah's 950 years down toward Abraham's 175 years.

Arpachshad was born "two years after the flood" (Gen 11:10), when Shem was 100 years old. This makes him the first named person born in the post-diluvian world, giving him a special position as a link between the old and the new world.

In rabbinic tradition (Jubilees 8:1–4), Arpachshad is associated with the regions east of the Euphrates, in what later became known as Chaldea. Some rabbinic sources attribute to him the role of one who preserved knowledge and traditions from before the flood.

Archaeological finds from Mesopotamia, especially from Tell Arpachiyah near Nineveh, have been attempted to be linked to the name Arpachshad, but this connection is debated among scholars. The area around northern Mesopotamia still fits well with the geographical location of Shem's descendants.
